newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sets up shelter for quake survivors, 554 dead.
newsitem.headline: Iran sets up shelter for quake survivors, 554 dead.

text.p: Iranian relief teams battling freezing temperatures set up temporary shelters on Sunday for over 35,000 people left homeless by an earthquake that killed 554 people in the country's mountainous northwest.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted Deputy Interior Minister Rasoul Zargar, who heads the relief operation, as saying the death toll climbed to 554 on Sunday morning.
It earlier said 4,000 relief workers were setting up temporary settlements to help the victims, who were given tents, blankets, heaters, bread, dates and canned fruit to survive.
Rescue teams on Saturday completed searches that were hampered by cold weather to save victims of the tremor that injured 2,000 people, IRNA added.
Zargar told Iranian television on Saturday that 719 of the injured had been admitted to hospitals.
The quake, measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale, hit the city of Ardabil and the town of Meshkinshahr at 4.27 p.m. (1257 GMT) on Friday, causing heavy damage to 110 neighbouring villages.
It was the deadliest of a series of earthquakes to shake the region.
Snowfall on Sunday slowed relief efforts, an Iranian Red Crescent official said.
Some 200 aftershocks - the strongest measuring 4.4 on the Richter scale -- had rocked Ardabil by Sunday morning, IRNA quoted officials as saying.

President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani called on authorities to bring speedy relief to stricken areas and urged people to send aid. Relief workers joined by residents set up 6,000 tents to shelter thousands of families, IRNA said.
Local authorities have announced three days of mourning in the province of Ardabil.

Ardabil is an agricultural province inhabited mainly by Iran's Azeri minority. It is one of Iran's coldest regions with freezing temperatures during the winter. Tehran Radio said snow in mountainous areas had hampered rescue operations.
Early on Saturday a tremor measuring about four on the Richter scale jolted an area near Bojnourd in northeastern Iran but caused no casualties or damage, IRNA said.
In early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in and around Bojnourd.
Force four and five tremors are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
Earthquakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in an area near the Caspian coast in 1990.
